Results and Efficiency

Experimental Protocol

The performance of the proposed LLR-based detector was evaluated within the binary hypothesis-testing framework:

\[ H_0: \text{“U-shape” of the yarn}, \qquad H_1: \text{hole or missing yarn}. \]

At each microswitch activation, the system acquires a cropped hook image, computes the log-likelihood ratio:

\[ LLR = s_{\text{pos}} - s_{\text{neg}}, \]

and compares it to a fixed threshold to decide between (H_0) and (H_1).

Dataset Split

To obtain an unbiased performance estimate, the dataset was divided into three non-overlapping subsets:

Subset Use Composition
Training set Positive/negative prototypes and discriminative ROI mask 39 positive and 27 negative images
Validation set Threshold selection and operating-point tuning 208 images
Test set Final independent evaluation 771 images

Threshold Selection with the Validation Set

With the initial threshold (LLR = 0), at least one false alarm occurred. Since a false alarm would unnecessarily stop the real machine, the threshold was adjusted following a Neyman–Pearson criterion, prioritizing a false-alarm rate as close as possible to zero.

The selected threshold was:

\[ LLR_{\text{thr}} = -0.035 \]

This threshold was then kept fixed during the final independent test.

Test-Set Performance

Predicted (H_0) Predicted (H_1)
True (H_0) — no defect TN = 633 FP = 0
True (H_1) — defect FN = 20 TP = 118

From these values:

\[ \text{Accuracy} = \frac{TP + TN}{TP + TN + FP + FN} = \frac{751}{771} \approx 97.4\% \]

\[ P_D = \frac{TP}{TP + FN} = \frac{118}{138} \approx 85.5\% \]

\[ P_F = \frac{FP}{FP + TN} \approx 0\%, \qquad \text{Specificity} \approx 100\% \]

The selected operating point therefore minimizes unnecessary stops while accepting a moderate number of missed detections.

Per-Colour Performance Analysis

Fuchsia Yarn — 373 images

Predicted (H_0) Predicted (H_1)
True (H_0) TN = 322 FP = 0
True (H_1) FN = 3 TP = 48

\[ \mathrm{ACC} \approx 99.2\%, \qquad \mathrm{TPR} \approx 94.1\%, \qquad \mathrm{FPR} \approx 0\% \]

Purple Yarn — 238 images

Predicted (H_0) Predicted (H_1)
True (H_0) TN = 193 FP = 0
True (H_1) FN = 8 TP = 37

\[ \mathrm{ACC} \approx 96.6\%, \qquad \mathrm{TPR} \approx 82.2\%, \qquad \mathrm{FPR} \approx 0\% \]

Light Blue Yarn — 160 images

Predicted (H_0) Predicted (H_1)
True (H_0) TN = 118 FP = 0
True (H_1) FN = 9 TP = 33

\[ \mathrm{ACC} \approx 94.4\%, \qquad \mathrm{TPR} \approx 78.6\%, \qquad \mathrm{FPR} \approx 0\% \]

The best performance is obtained for the fuchsia yarn. The light blue yarn has the lowest detection probability, since its grayscale appearance is closer to the background and it creates less contrast in the region of interest.

Out-of-Distribution Failure Case

A pale pink yarn was considered as an out-of-distribution case, since it was not included in training, validation or test sets. In this condition, more than 32% of samples were misclassified and the (H_0) and (H_1) LLR distributions overlapped substantially.

This result indicates that extremely low-contrast yarn/background combinations lie outside the current operating domain and require more robust or learned features.

Real-Time Operation on Raspberry Pi 3

The complete acquisition and detection pipeline runs directly on the Raspberry Pi 3 and is triggered by the synchronization event. During the error-recognition experiments, the event interval was approximately (0.42,), corresponding to an inspection rate of:

\[ f_{\text{inspect}} \approx 2.4 \ \text{inspections/s} \]

At each trigger, a full-resolution image is captured, cropped to a (76 ) region of interest and processed through preprocessing, normalized cross-correlation scoring and LLR evaluation.

The processing time remains below the interval between consecutive synchronization events. The available computational margin also enables future multi-frame decision fusion strategies, such as majority voting or LLR averaging.
